If you're working with Uniface 10.4, you'll encounter the setocc statement frequently. This powerful command helps you navigate through database records in your application. Let's break it down in simple terms! 📊
The setocc statement stands for "set occurrence" and it makes a specific database record the currently active one. Think of it like selecting a row in a spreadsheet - you're telling Uniface "I want to work with this specific record right now."
setocc Entity, OccurrenceNumber

  Entity: The name of your database table or entity (like "CUSTOMER" or "ORDER")

Transport Layer Security (TLS) is the backbone of modern web security, but a mis‑configured Nginx server can still expose your site to downgrade attacks, weak ciphers, or information leakage. TLS 1.3 offers forward secrecy by default and reduces handshake round‑trips. Disable everything older than TLS 1.2.

articles.author: Muhammad Mairaj
articles.description:
AI demos are intoxicating.
They make you feel like the future has arrived.
A few clicks, a few prompts, and suddenly you are looking at something that feels like science fiction.
But here’s the problem.
The same demo that dazzles on stage almost always collapses when you try to turn it into a product.
Why?
Because a demo is theater, and production is reality.
A demo is built to impress, not to last.
It only shows the happy path.
The presenter knows what to type.
They avoid the weird edge cases.
The inputs are clean, the timing is perfect, and the audience only sees the system at its best.
Production is the opposite.
Real users are unpredictable.
They type half-formed thoughts, use slang, and ask things the system was never designed to handle.
If the demo is a polished photo, production is …
articles.title: Why most AI demos fail in production
